what: The one list the /workshop/ page draws itself from. Every area is a branch, every entry a leaf. A lane that ships a page appends one leaf here (node scripts/workshop-add.mjs) and the page is current; nobody edits workshop/index.html by hand.

items.title: Statistics · bottoms, the 200-day, the rising tide
items.blurb: The VIX turns with the low or just before it. Deep below the 200-day went on to fall a median 12% more, about twice what chance gives. The tide is real; today's is narrow.

items.title: Comps · labels on the chart (MU, P/E trailing)
items.blurb: One football-field row read like an Excel chart: lowest and highest peer at the line ends, 25th/75th at the box edges, the median, MU today ($1,071 at 24.2x). TSM and SIMO fail a data check and are marked in red.

items.title: Comps · labels, round 2 (one clean row)
items.blurb: One football-field row drawn once, as for a board meeting: the row header on the left, six numbers on the chart (line ends, box edges, median, MU today), the dollar values stacked on the right. The same design on four rows (P/E trailing, EV/EBITDA, P/S, P/E forward). No tickers on the chart, no dots, no outlier variants.
items.ask: THIS ROW DESIGN FOR THE TABLE?

items.title: Fund valuation · P/E and total earnings
items.blurb: Computed from holdings (FMP gives no ETF P/E): SPY 26.1x, QQQ 37.3x; IWM's companies lose more than they earn in total, 16.2x counting only the profitable. No NAV premium: FMP's nav is undated.

items.title: Hub bundle · INDEXES bow tie, earnings REACTION, EARNINGS tab, USUAL DAY top-up, study charts
items.blurb: Index funds get their own bow tie under SECTORS; the earnings room's past reports show the next-session move; the company tab reads EARNINGS; the studies index shows each study's headline chart; USUAL DAY's history tops itself up each night once deployed; prediction markets gain 23 Polymarket topics that roll at expiry.

items.title: Statistics · market leaders and rotation
items.blurb: Since 2020 the top ten contributors gave about two-thirds of each up year's gain. Leaders did not look special beforehand. Rotating into one calmer name trimmed pain a little; a basket halved it.

items.title: Market map · round 3 · the tree
items.blurb: The Geiger is a bar under every ball; funds carry a second striped bar for their holdings, with a divergence line on the card. Click the same ball again to let go. Read top-down: flat at the top, 3D lower where the names need room.

items.title: Market map round 3 · what changed
items.blurb: Before and after at 1680 and 390: the bar Geiger, the holdings blend, let go, the top-down tree. The 27 Sep wheel is unchanged.

items.title: Statistics · market regime, six questions
items.blurb: Equal vs cap weight, the VIX curve, credit, 10-year and dollar with the high-yield-pullback thesis, seasonality, the Fed and prediction-market odds for 28 Oct.

items.title: Proposal · a market regime strip on the Hub
items.blurb: Seven gauges in one row (breadth, fear curve, credit, 10-year, dollar, calendar, Fed), each flashing only at its own most extreme 5%. Nothing built.

items.title: Prediction markets · what the betting markets expect
items.blurb: Polymarket's odds on the Fed and other central banks, yields, inflation prints, recession, Japan and the carry trade, China–Taiwan, oil, Iran, Ukraine, tariffs, Washington, AI and the midterms, read every 15 minutes in US hours. A workshop page, not a Hub tab; Kalshi stays off. The 23 added topics and the automatic move to the next market when one expires are on branch candidate/hub-bundle-20260928, not yet deployed.

items.title: Put/call audit · is it accurate?
items.blurb: The arithmetic lands within 1-2% of Cboe, but 21 names went silent after a Gateway blink, 122 Hub names are not on the reader's list, and the 'index' line is really SPY+QQQ+IWM. Measured Monday morning.

items.title: Statistics · RSI on the full history
items.blurb: S&P to 1928, Nasdaq, VIX, oil, gold and more. SPY's bottom 10% is RSI 39.5 or lower; what followed was not reliably better than any day, and it usually dipped a little first.

items.title: Statistics · RSI ladder, every rung 1 to 100
items.blurb: No forced 10%: every percentile, every pullback. Bitcoin's RSI goes deeper and more often (bottom 1% at 23.3 vs SPY 28.7). 'Lower rung, better next 20 sessions' holds in US stocks since 2004, not 1928-2003.

items.title: Proposal · a scout tier for names off the Hub
items.blurb: A cheap third tier that screens every US stock nightly from data we already get in bulk; a name moves up only when you promote it.

items.title: Scout · IWM small caps, screened
items.blurb: All 1,988 IWM holdings through filters you can change, most oversold first. Of the 31 we carry: 5 in the bottom 20% of their own RSI history, 22 below their 200-day, 4 with positive earnings.
